classes.name: Apple___Apple_scab
classes.symptoms: Dull olive-green or brown velvety spots on leaves, puckered surfaces, premature leaf drop.
precautions: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to disrupt fungal overwintering
Prune tree canopy during dormancy to maximize sunlight penetration and air movement
Avoid overhead irrigation to minimize leaf wetness duration
Select disease-resistant apple cultivars for future plantings
classes.treatment: Apply sulfur or copper-based fungicide sprays during early bud break. Rake and dispose of fallen infected leaves.

classes.name: Apple___Black_rot
classes.symptoms: Frog-eye circular leaf spots with purple margins and tan centers, black rotting mummified fruit.
precautions: Remove mummified rotting fruit clinging to branches or ground
Prune out dead wood, fire-blight strikes, and cankered limbs
Disinfect pruning shears between cuts using 70% isopropyl alcohol
Maintain tree vigor with balanced organic fertilizers
classes.treatment: Prune out dead wood and fire-blight strikes. Apply captan or mancozeb fungicides as recommended.

classes.name: Apple___healthy
classes.symptoms: Vibrant green leaves, unblemished smooth surface, robust foliage.
precautions: Continue regular orchard scouting for early pest detection
Maintain balanced drip hydration and soil moisture levels
Conduct periodic soil pH and nutrient testing
Apply dormant horticultural oil in late winter for preventative pest management
classes.treatment: Maintain balanced fertilization, regular irrigation, and periodic pest monitoring.

classes.name: Corn___Common_rust
classes.symptoms: Cinnamon-brown oval to elongate powdery pustules scattered over upper and lower leaf surfaces.
precautions: Plant resistant corn hybrids with proven rust resistance genes
Plant early in the season to evade peak late-summer spore arrival
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization which produces soft, susceptible foliage
Monitor weather forecasts for prolonged humid, mild conditions
classes.treatment: Plant resistant corn hybrids. Apply foliar triazole or strobilurin fungicides if infection develops early.

classes.name: Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight
classes.symptoms: Long, elliptical grayish-green or tan lesions (cigar-shaped) expanding parallel to leaf veins.
precautions: Practice a 2-year crop rotation with non-host crops like soybeans
Incorporate or deep-till previous crop residue into soil
Space plants adequately to reduce canopy humidity
Select hybrids with multi-gene quantitative resistance
classes.treatment: Utilize crop rotation with non-host crops, till residue, and use fungicide treatments at first onset.

classes.name: Corn___healthy
classes.symptoms: Uniform deep green color, intact leaf margins, no fungal pustules or discoloration.
precautions: Maintain side-dress nitrogen schedule according to crop stage
Scout field perimeters for weed hosts that harbor pathogens
Ensure optimal field drainage to avoid root stress
classes.treatment: Ensure adequate nitrogen supply, monitor soil moisture, and scout regularly for root pests.

classes.name: Potato___Early_blight
classes.symptoms: Concentric rings producing a 'target board' effect surrounded by yellow chlorotic halos on mature leaves.
precautions: Remove and burn infected plant debris after harvest
Use certified disease-free seed tubers from verified suppliers
Apply mulch around stems to inhibit soil splash infection
Water early in the morning using drip irrigation rather than sprinklers
classes.treatment: Apply chlorothalonil or copper-based sprays every 7-10 days. Ensure drip irrigation to minimize leaf wetness.

classes.name: Potato___Late_blight
classes.symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions that rapidly expand and turn brown/black with white fuzzy growth underneath.
precautions: Eliminate cull potato piles and volunteer potatoes near fields
Ensure high soil hilling over developing tubers to block spore wash-in
Avoid working in field rows when foliage is wet from dew or rain
Destroy vines 2-3 weeks before harvest to prevent tuber contamination
classes.treatment: Eliminate cull piles, use certified disease-free seed tubers, and treat with metalaxyl/cymoxanil formulations.

classes.name: Potato___healthy
classes.symptoms: Healthy dark-green compound leaves, vigorous canopy without necrotic patches.
precautions: Rotate crops on a strict 3-year rotation away from nightshades
Keep hills properly mounded around plant bases
Monitor soil moisture to prevent drought stress and tuber cracking
classes.treatment: Keep well-hilled soil, rotate crops on a 3-year cycle, and manage soil moisture levels.

classes.name: Tomato___Bacterial_spot
classes.symptoms: Small, water-soaked, dark brown circular lesions with greasy appearance and yellow borders.
precautions: Treat seeds with hot water (50°C for 25 minutes) before sowing
Avoid handling or pruning tomato vines when foliage is wet
Sterilize stakes, cages, and tools between growing seasons
Use drip lines instead of overhead sprinklers
classes.treatment: Spray fixed copper mixed with mancozeb. Avoid overhead watering and avoid handling wet plants.

classes.name: Tomato___Early_blight
classes.symptoms: Brown spots on leaves with concentric target-board rings and progressive defoliation from lower foliage.
precautions: Remove affected leaves immediately to reduce spore spread
Improve air circulation by pruning lower 12 inches of foliage and staking vines
Avoid overhead watering; use ground-level drip irrigation
Apply organic straw mulch around plant bases to prevent soil splashing
classes.treatment: Mulch soil around plants, prune bottom 12 inches of foliage, and apply bio-fungicide Bacillus subtilis or copper.

classes.name: Tomato___Late_blight
classes.symptoms: Large, irregular greasy dark water-soaked blotches on leaves and stems that turn brown and collapse.
precautions: Inspect plants frequently during cool, wet, humid weather
Isolate and bag severely infected plants before removal to prevent airborne spread
Never compost infected tomato foliage; bag and dispose off-site
Ensure wide plant spacing (24-36 inches) for rapid morning drying
classes.treatment: Remove and incinerate severely infected plants immediately. Apply protective copper soap sprays preventative.

classes.name: Tomato___healthy
classes.symptoms: Lush emerald-green leaves, crisp leaflets, strong stems with no leaf spots or curling.
precautions: Maintain consistent drip watering to prevent blossom end rot
Stake or cage plants to keep foliage off ground level
Apply balanced organic compost rich in calcium and potassium
Scout weekly under leaf undersides for aphid and whitefly vectors
classes.treatment: Maintain optimal staking, consistent drip hydration, calcium-rich soil, and regular scouting.
